result.title: TRACK: Multiple Instance Learning for Anti-Money Laundering in Transaction Networks
result.comment: 11 pages, 3 figures. Accepted at the 20th ACM International Conference on Web Search and Data Mining (WSDM 2027)
result.summary: Anti-money laundering (AML) investigations are organized around accounts, while the suspicious evidence for an account may reside in only a few of its transactions. Yet many account-level detectors summarize transactions before learning, and message-passing models may aggregate once more over neighboring accounts. We name this discrepancy the aggregation mismatch and study it under an account-window benchmark label defined by the presence of at least one flagged transaction. We recast account-level AML detection as multiple instance learning, in which an account-window is a bag and its transactions are instances. We propose TRACK, which encodes every transaction with a shared encoder and selectively pools the encodings into an account decision. To emulate coarse supervision, we withhold the transaction labels of five AML datasets from TRACK throughout training. Under a time-ordered protocol, TRACK achieves the highest average precision among the tabular and graph baselines trained from account labels on every dataset. Despite using only account-window supervision, it remains competitive with edge classifiers trained directly from transaction labels. Its instance scores also rank flagged transactions well above chance and approach or exceed directly supervised ranking performance across datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将账户级反洗钱检测重构为多示例学习：账户窗口是 bag、交易是 instance，提出 TRACK 用共享编码器逐笔编码再选择性池化成账户决策，训练中刻意不使用交易级标签。
AI.relevance_reason: 「粗粒度 bag 监督下从大量实例中挑出少数关键证据、并给出实例级分数」的问题表述，可能与 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选和 latent 贡献分配相呼应，但领域与模态相距较远，仅供概念核查。
